tigate; for the proper work of **Cold** is **Condensation**; and it is accomplished without any malignancy or hostile quality: and therefore the operation is safer than through **Opiates**; although it is a little less powerful, if it were used only occasionally, as **Opiates** are used. But again, because it can be used familiarly and moderately in the daily diet, it is even far more powerful for the **Prolongation of life** than through **Opiates**.

<margin>39</margin> The **Cooling of the Spirits** is done in three ways: either through **Respiration**; or through **Vapors**; or through **Aliments** <gloss>food and drink</gloss>. The first is the best, but is almost beyond our power; the second is also powerful, and yet it is at hand; the third is weak and works through circuits <note>meaning it takes a longer, indirect route through the digestive system</note>.

**Air** <note>Catchword for the following page</note>

<summary>Bacon argues that using cold to condense the vital spirits is safer than using opiates and can be more effective for longevity when incorporated into a daily diet. He identifies breathing, vapors, and food as the three methods for cooling the spirits.</summary>
<keywords>cold, condensation, prolongation of life, cooling of spirits, respiration, vapors, diet, vital spirits</keywords>
